description: PRD-268 (docs/PRDS/PRD-268-PROACTIVE-AUTO.md) wave W1: US-C01–C07, US-C17 and US-C18, re-cut into 19 one-session stories in dependency order. Core only (no frontend); ONE Alembic revision (prd268_w1_proactive); no new dependency; no third-party client. Diff base for every check: `bash scripts/ralph/acceptance-prd268w1.sh --print-base`.
decisions: K1 Branch and PR. All work happens on feat/prd-268-w1-check-ins in <workspace>/.worktrees/automatos-ai/feat+prd-268-w1-check-ins. The branch is cut from RALPH_BASE_REF: origin/main once PR #1362 (the PRD) has merged, else origin/docs/prd-268-proactive-auto. One PR for the wave (base main, closes tracking issue #1358) and one CI run at the end.
K2 Story order is the dependency order (the `priority` field), and each story gets one session. A story never waits on CI.

K3 Files over 800 lines never grow. Where a story must add lines to one, it moves at least as many lines out in the same commit, to a new module, re-exported when tests import it. Before moving a name, grep orchestrator/tests for `<module>.<name>` patch targets; a name a test patches by module path stays put. The files: services/heartbeat_service.py 1825, modules/tools/discovery/platform_executor.py 1543, modules/tools/execution/unified_executor.py 1390, main.py 1666, modules/agents/factory/agent_factory.py 1982, api/missions.py 2107, api/board_tasks.py 2282, services/activity_service.py 1267, core/llm/manager.py 1063. Re-measure each. The exceptions: orchestrator/config.py gains its settings lines, and route-manifest.json and config-surface.json gain their entries.

K4 Never touch a line inside a function over 50 code lines (scripts/ci/check_changed_code_shape.py fails every touched line inside one). The seams that don't count: a decorator line above `def` (PlatformActionExecutor.clear already has one), a new short function, a new module, a line in a short function (schedule_agent_heartbeat and schedule_orchestrator_heartbeat are short). The gate compares these functions byte for byte with the base: HeartbeatService._agent_tick, _orchestrator_tick, _orchestrator_tick_llm, _dispatch_heartbeat_notification, _route_heartbeat_to_auto, PlatformActionExecutor.clear and PlatformActionExecutor._run_cleared.

K5 This Mac cannot import the orchestrator. route-manifest.json and config-surface.json are edited by hand or with a stdlib-only python snippet, in the format of scripts/dump_routes.py: routes sorted by (path, method), route_count equal to the number of routes, written as json.dumps(..., indent=2, sort_keys=True) + newline. Setting names go in sorted position.

K6 Exactly one Alembic revision, prd268_w1_proactive, chained onto the current head (re-read EXPECTED_HEAD in orchestrator/tests/test_prd209_alembic_single_head.py; it was prd266_w2_push on 28 Oct). It uses CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS and moves both pins: test_prd209_alembic_single_head.py (the comment chain plus EXPECTED_HEAD) and test_prd236_w1_routes.py (read the new file, assert its down_revision, update the EXPECTED_HEAD line).

K7 Rollout. The proactive mode is off | shadow | live: a platform system setting (category `proactive`, key `mode`), read strictly, with config PROACTIVE_MODE_DEFAULT='off'. A failed read means off, like Socials (modules/socials/settings.py:108-133). In shadow, today's heartbeats run unchanged and check-ins run beside them, recording suggestions. In live, check_in agents and the orchestrator heartbeat at proactive_level silent or notify run check-ins INSTEAD of today's tick. W1 ships no delivery (W2 brings it), so live stays off until W2; the code supports it now and the tests cover it.

K8 The check-in runner owns its tool loop; it never goes through AgentFactory. It offers only read platform actions plus platform_suggest_next_step, and runs every call through PlatformActionExecutor.execute with caller_context lane='check_in', the run id and the run's read log. Composio, plugins, the Anthropic memory tool, sub-agents, Missions and platform_execute are never offered. A decorator on PlatformActionExecutor.clear refuses any call in the lane that isn't positively `read`, unknown actions included (defence in depth). A decorator on UnifiedToolExecutor.execute_tool refuses any non-platform tool in the lane.

K9 Model and caps. Every check-in calls LLMManager(service_name='heartbeat'), the platform orchestrator_llm system setting (default claude-haiku-5-5). An agent's own model_config is not used in the check-in lane. Per run: at most 4 tool iterations, 800 output tokens, 12,000 tokens of context and $0.05; past the ceiling the run stops and records `error`.

K10 Heartbeat mode. heartbeat.mode is check_in | act. When unset: act if the heartbeat's auto_act is true, else check_in (PRD §12-Q1). An agent whose work needs connector reads (Composio) can't do them in a check-in, which fails closed; its owner keeps it `act`. CLI-agent heartbeats (file_cli_ticket, one open per agent) are unchanged in W1. The Run-now routes (run_agent_heartbeat, run_orchestrator_heartbeat) keep today's tick.
K11 The addressee of a suggestion is the workspace owner (§12-Q2).

K12 Start kinds in W1: board_task and chat. The schema accepts mission and playbook_run, but Start answers 409 'not available in this version' for them until US-C14 (W4), where check-ins first propose them. W1's check-in prompts propose board_task or chat only.

K13 Language. Server-written copy (next_step sentences, run notes, refusal text) comes from strings tables in English and Portuguese (Brazil), chosen by the request's Accept-Language (en default). No stored preference in W1. Background copy uses en.

K14 Spend. The lane string 'check_in' joins BACKGROUND_LANES (services/credits/asks.py:38), so a trial never pays for it. background_allowed (services/credits/routing.py:170) and daily_spend_guard.refuse_new_work are checked at every run start. The ceiling is off (0) by default and fails open, so tests set one.

K15 Audit. AuditService.log commits the caller's session (core/workspaces/audit.py:97). Call it after the atomic status UPDATE has committed, or in its own session; never inside the Start or Hide transaction.

K16 Approvals. Gerard approved PRD-268 on 28 Oct 2026 ("get it all started"; tracking issue #1358). This wave adds a guardrail (the lane), changes heartbeat behaviour in live mode and governs background spend: build exactly what the ACs say.

K17 Mislabelled actions. Every action states its level. platform_field_inject writes (handlers_field.py:119) and becomes `write`, with its hierarchy-gate entry (scripts/check_hierarchy_gate.py: _HIERARCHY_TARGETS, admin_only, or ALLOW_LIST with a reason). A read action the sweep catches writing is relabelled, never excepted.
ownerTest: Shadow week, step 0 (PRD §10): set the platform system setting proactive.mode = shadow, then settings.proactive.enabled = true on Gerard's workspace and c1 (PUT /api/proactive/settings). Over the week compare GET /api/proactive/runs with the tickets the heartbeats filed. Live stays off until W2 delivers.
Read 20 random proactive_runs rows: silent runs have zero llm_usage rows; suggested runs cite reads the run made.
Confirm the read-only lane on SaaS: a check-in transcript shows no write tool offered (the run's tool list), and the lane refusal never fired against a legitimate read.

acceptanceCriteria: New test orchestrator/tests/test_prd268_read_actions_write_nothing.py calls every registered read action's handler with parameters synthesised from its JSON schema (required fields with minimal valid values), against a session whose add, delete, flush, commit and execute of INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE are recorded, and an outbound HTTP transport (httpx and requests) that records; it asserts zero writes per action and names each action that wrote. Each call runs against spy_session (MagicMock(spec=Session) over an empty database; records add, add_all, delete, merge, flush, commit, bulk_*, Query.update/delete, and execute/scalar/scalars of INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, DDL, pg_notify, nextval, on the session, its connection and its engine) and under recording_http (httpx.HTTPTransport.handle_request, httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport.handle_async_request and requests.adapters.HTTPAdapter.send patched to record and answer 200 {}). userStories.title: Read-labelled actions that write are offered and cleared in a check-in: relabel them, or make them read (K17)
userStories.description: As an owner, I need 'read' to mean read in the check-in lane, so a background check-in never commits a write (PRD-268 §6.2.3, FR-1, K17; review finding, HIGH). The lane clears any action registered as read (check_in_lane.may_clear_in_a_check_in / offered_in_a_check_in), and several read actions write on a path a check-in reaches with a real workspace's data. US-C02d's own evidence lists them as 'open for the owner, not relabelled because the empty-database sweep cannot reach them', which excepts them, and K17 says a read action that writes is relabelled, never excepted.
acceptanceCriteria: Cause, confirmed in the code: (a) platform_search_packages (actions_packages.py, read) calls handlers_packages._record_offer_if_onboarding, which runs onboarding_state.record_package_event(..., commit=True) on the executor's session: in a workspace whose onboarding stage is not terminal, a check-in rewrites workspaces.settings.onboarding.funnel and commits; (b) platform_codegraph_search and platform_codegraph_get_symbol (actions_codegraph.py, read) reach codegraph_service._log_query, which INSERTs a codegraph_query_logs row and commits; (c) platform_read_document (actions_read_document.py, read) calls services.spreadsheet_workspace.workspace_copies, which writes a spreadsheet's copy into the workspace when it is missing; (d) the rest of US-C02d's own list: platform_query_data (audit and training rows), platform_search_documents (telemetry and last_accessed through its own sessions); and, latent (inert in the lane today because no session ticket is injected), platform_render_preview, which writes into a session folder when one is. The empty-database sweep (tests/test_prd268_read_actions_write_nothing.py) cannot see any of these: the data that triggers each write is absent, and writes on a session the handler opens itself bypass spy_session. → DONE — confirmed in the code: (a) handlers_packages._record_offer_if_onboarding calls onboarding_state.record_package_event(commit=True), whose _persist adds the workspace and commits; (b) CodeGraphService.search_symbols and semantic_search end in _log_query, an INSERT INTO codegraph_query_logs and a commit; (c) handlers_documents.read_document calls spreadsheet_workspace.workspace_copies, which lists the workspace and writes the missing copy over HTTP to the workspace worker; (d) platform_query_data (exec_research.run_nl2sql): _audit writes a DatabaseQueryAudit row on a session of its own, query_database's auto_train stores an NL2SQL training example, _emit_nl2sql_primitive writes a heartbeat_results row, and (found in this story's security review) get_similar_examples bumps usage_count and last_used_at on every few-shot example it hands out and commits; platform_search_documents: RAGService._track_document_access updates documents.last_accessed on a thread with its own session, and record_substrate_search_nowait inserts a substrate_metric_events row through the executor (the memory searches insert that row too, even on an error); platform_render_preview writes its PNG into sessions/<ticket>/ once a session ticket is injected. The empty-database sweep saw none: each is reached only when something exists, and most write on a session the code opens itself. Commit ac66e0ec8

Change: each action in (a)–(d) either becomes permission_level='write' with its hierarchy-gate entry (scripts/check_hierarchy_gate.py: _HIERARCHY_TARGETS, admin_only, or ALLOW_LIST with a reason), or its handler stops writing so the 'read' label is true (for example, the telemetry or funnel write is skipped when caller_context is a check-in's, or moved out of the read path). None is excepted. Record per action which was chosen and why (Strict mode asks before a write in chat, so relabelling a document read changes chat behaviour; that is the trade-off to state). → DONE — none relabelled: each action stays read and writes nothing in a check-in. core/read_only_call.py holds the scope (reading_only, only_reading: a ContextVar that the tasks, asyncio.to_thread and core.best_effort threads a call starts inherit); check_in_lane.carries_the_check_in runs every check-in call except platform_suggest_next_step inside it. Per action: platform_search_packages skips the funnel stamp (a check-in's search is no offer to anyone); platform_codegraph_search and platform_codegraph_get_symbol skip the query log (modules/codegraph/query_log.py log_query, moved out of codegraph_service.py, 1862 to 1836 lines); platform_read_document gets no spreadsheet copy (workspace_copies answers None in a check-in: no listing, no copy, so the read loses workspace_path and row_count for a spreadsheet, and a check-in runs no code on a copy anyway); platform_query_data writes no audit row (_audit), trains nothing (_ask passes auto_train=False; SQLExampleStore.add_example stores nothing in a check-in, which also covers smart_query and analyze_database), emits no heartbeat (_emit_nl2sql_primitive) and counts no few-shot use (_count_the_use); platform_search_documents skips the access stamp (modules/rag/access_tracking.py, moved out of rag/service.py, 1728 to 1704 lines) and the substrate event (record_substrate_search and record_substrate_search_nowait both ask before the run_in_executor hop, which does not carry the context; this also covers platform_search_memory and the other memory searches); platform_render_preview refuses before drawing (NOT_IN_A_CHECK_IN). Why not relabel: Strict asks before every write in chat, so a document, data or code read would wait for a card; receipts (turn_account.is_read) and follows_the_owner would count each as a change; the platform_write rate limit would be spent on reads; and check-ins would lose documents and data. Trade-off for the owner: a check-in's NL2SQL query lands no database_query_audit row, so PRD-160 S4's one audit row per NL query now excludes check-ins (the run is in proactive_runs, without its SQL); the security reviewer recommended keeping read and skipping the row. The two moved writers now log a failure with logger.exception (AGENTS.md), louder than the old debug and warning. Commit ac66e0ec8

Test: the sweep is extended so it would have caught these: seed what triggers each write (a workspace mid-onboarding with a matching package, a codegraph project with a matching symbol, a spreadsheet document without its workspace copy, a data source for platform_query_data), and record writes on sessions the handler opens itself (patch core.database.database.SessionLocal to hand out spy sessions) and file writes into the workspace. The extended sweep fails on the commit before this story and passes after it. A lane test proves each relabelled action is neither offered (offered_in_a_check_in) nor cleared (may_clear_in_a_check_in), and each made-read action writes nothing when run through PlatformActionExecutor.execute with caller_context lane='check_in'. → DONE — tests/test_prd268_read_actions_write_nothing.py: the sweep now calls each read handler as a check-in (reading_only) with own_sessions (core.database.database.SessionLocal hands out sessions that record every write and refuse every read, so no process cache keeps an empty answer); a write into the workspace is an httpx request to the worker, which recording_http records. Seeded cases (tests/helpers_check_in_seeds.py SEEDS: a matching package mid-onboarding, an indexed codegraph project, a spreadsheet without its workspace copy, a connected database, a document search that finds a passage, a preview with a session ticket): test_a_seeded_read_action_writes_nothing_in_a_check_in and test_a_seeded_read_action_reaches_its_record_outside_a_check_in (each seed's marks: the funnel commit, the codegraph INSERT, the HTTP POST to the worker, add(AuditRow) and add(TrainingExample), UPDATE documents and add(SubstrateMetricEvent)), test_every_seeded_action_is_a_read_a_check_in_may_run, and self-tests test_a_session_the_handler_opens_itself_is_watched, test_a_session_the_handler_opens_itself_answers_no_read, test_a_write_into_the_workspace_is_seen, test_a_seeded_session_finds_what_it_holds_and_still_records_writes. tests/test_prd268_read_actions_in_a_check_in.py (new): test_each_made_read_action_writes_nothing_through_the_executor_in_a_check_in (each seed through PlatformActionExecutor.execute with caller_context lane='check_in': no write, and its expected answer), test_the_lane_runs_each_check_in_call_reading_only, test_the_suggestion_is_the_one_check_in_call_not_reading_only, test_reading_only_marks_the_block_and_the_work_it_starts, test_a_check_in_query_emits_no_nl2sql_heartbeat, test_a_check_in_query_stores_no_training_example, test_a_check_in_query_counts_no_use_of_an_example, test_a_check_in_search_records_no_substrate_event. No action was relabelled, so the relabel half of the lane test has nothing to cover (platform_field_query, relabelled in US-C02d, keeps its tests). On the commit before this story the new tests fail (no core.read_only_call, and each seeded call wrote in the lane). tests/test_prd154_s8_codegraph.py reads the INSERT's columns from query_log.py now (same assertions). code-reviewer: fixed that test (HIGH); security-reviewer: fixed the example store's use count and add_example (MEDIUM). Not run locally (this Mac cannot import the orchestrator); CI runs them at the end of the wave, and the stronger sweep may surface a read action not traced here. Commit ac66e0ec8
userStories.notes: Review finding (security-reviewer MEDIUM-1, raised to HIGH: it is the wave's guardrail, and K17 already decided relabel-never-except). Verified: handlers_packages.py:108,133; codegraph_service.py:1371-1405; handlers_documents.py:525-528 (workspace_copies). K3/K4 apply: handlers over 50 lines are not touched inside; add a short function or a decorator. platform_field_query (US-C02d) is the precedent for a relabel and its knock-ons.

userStories.title: Building a check-in's context reinforces the workspace field: the CHECK_IN field_memory read records no access
userStories.description: As an owner, I need a check-in to change nothing, including the vector field (PRD-268 §6.2.3, FR-1; review finding, MEDIUM). ContextMode.CHECK_IN (modes.py, this wave) includes the field_memory section. FieldMemorySection._query_workspace_field calls VectorFieldSharedContext.query_workspace, which runs _scored_search with record_access=True: Hebbian reinforcement (_reinforce_batch updates access_count, last_accessed and strength) on every pattern it returns, and ensure_shared_collection may create the collection. That is the same write US-C02d relabelled platform_field_query as a write for, and it happens on every check-in in ContextService.build_context, before the lane sees any call, so patterns a check-in reads stop decaying.
acceptanceCriteria: Cause: modules/context/adapters/vector_field.py query_workspace takes no record_access and always reinforces; modules/context/sections/field_memory.py calls it the same way in every mode. → DONE — confirmed: VectorFieldSharedContext.query_workspace had no record_access and called _scored_search with its default True, so _scored_search_inner ran _reinforce_batch (set_payload of access_count, last_accessed and strength) on every pattern it returned; FieldMemorySection._query_workspace_field called it the same way in every mode, CHECK_IN included, in ContextService.build_context before the lane sees any call. Commit 8462616f0

Commit 8462616f0

userStories.title: Open suggestions never expire at expires_at: lapsed rows stay startable, block dedupe and hold an agent at its open cap
userStories.description: As an owner running the shadow week, I need a suggestion to lapse after 7 days as §6.2.4 says, so an agent whose three suggestions nobody answered can suggest again and a stale suggestion cannot be started (PRD-268 §6.2.4 'Open suggestions expire after 7 days', §6.9; review finding, MEDIUM). platform_suggest_next_step writes expires_at = created_at + 7 days, but nothing reads it: the only paths to 'expired' are the open-per-person overflow (_make_room) and a streak's success. In W1 nobody sees the suggestions (no delivery, no frontend), so during the shadow week every agent reaches max_open_per_agent (3) and every later suggestion of that agent is refused, its check-ins still spending a model call; a subject once suggested is blocked by dedupe for good; GET /api/proactive/suggestions lists month-old rows as open; and Start files a ticket from a lapsed one.
acceptanceCriteria: Cause: services/proactive/decisions.py _require_open checks status only; services/proactive/limits.py open_for_agent and handlers_proactive._duplicate count every status='open' row; services/proactive/listing.py lists them; no code moves an open row past its expires_at to expired.

Change: one function (for example services/proactive/expiry.py expire_lapsed(db, workspace_id, now)) runs one UPDATE proactive_suggestions SET status='expired' WHERE workspace_id = :ws AND status = 'open' AND expires_at <= :now, workspace-scoped; it runs at every check-in start before the caps and the dedupe read (the runner's prepare), and in Start, Hide and the list before they read; a Start or Hide of a lapsed row answers 409 expired and files nothing. A streak card's expires_at keeps being pushed on while the agent fails (failing_streaks), so a live streak never lapses.

Test (realdb): an open suggestion 8 days old is expired at the next check-in and no longer counts toward max_open_per_agent or dedupe (the agent can suggest the same subject again); Start of a lapsed row is 409 expired with no ticket; GET ?status=open omits it and ?status=expired lists it; a 6-day-old row is untouched; another workspace's lapsed rows are not touched; the tests fail on the commit before this story.
userStories.notes: Review finding (code-reviewer MEDIUM, confirmed by security-reviewer LOW-1). No W1 AC names the lapse, but §6.2.4 defines it and the shadow week (ownerTest step 0) is skewed without it. Raising a suggestion_changed event on expiry stays W2 (US-C08). If the owner prefers this in W2, it is the owner's call to move it; until then it is open here.

userStories.title: The proactive routes' 503 path logs only the exception's class: log the detail
userStories.description: As an operator, I need the server log to carry what failed when a suggestion or settings route answers 503 (AGENTS.md 'Errors and inputs': the detail goes to the server log; review finding, LOW). api/proactive.py _unavailable logs logger.error('proactive %s failed: %s', what, type(failure).__name__): a database error on list, Start, Hide or the settings writes leaves no message and no stack.
acceptanceCriteria: Cause: api/proactive.py _unavailable (line ~196) logs type(failure).__name__ only.

Change: _unavailable logs with the exception's message and stack (logger.error(..., exc_info=failure) or logger.exception inside the except), keeping the response unchanged (the same refusal code, 503, no internals in the body).
Test: a route whose service raises SQLAlchemyError answers 503 with the same body, and the captured log record carries exc_info (caplog); the test fails on the commit before this story.
